original_question: How high can a human throw something?
submitted_by: Irish Dave on the Isle of Man
short_answer_summary: The author estimates around 70 m for an elite baseball throw and perhaps 80 m for a golf ball, assuming speed can be directed vertically.
detailed_scientific_explanation: Humans are unusually accurate throwers; release timing must be tighter than nerve travel times, showing the importance of coordinated predictive movement. Because people throw forward more effectively than upward, the author allows a passive device that redirects velocity vertically without adding energy. Aerodynamic calculations for baseballs give heights in 5 m giraffe units: ordinary throw three, good arm five, 80 mph pitcher ten, and Aroldis Chapman's 105 mph pitch fourteen. A golf ball might be better: lighter mass may reduce elbow-torque limits and allow higher speed, while its flight properties support an estimated sixteen giraffes. Roald Bradstock's varied-object throwing provides empirical motivation. Tools that actively add speed are excluded; a buoyant balloon is the ending loophole.
initial_assumptions: Bare-handed launch energy; passive redirection allowed

quantitative_facts.value: Half-millisecond release error can miss strike zone; fastest nerve transit along arm ~5 ms
1 giraffe=5 m; average 3 giraffes=15 m; good arm 5=25 m
Bradstock golf-ball distance 170 yd; hypothesized vertical elite golf throw 16 giraffes≈80 m

uncertainties_and_limitations: Maximum is approximate; little throwing-speed data for alternative projectiles
Historical pitch record not current claim
extraction_notes: Source transcript is machine OCR and requires line-by-line proofreading against page images.
